transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me today. Um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I guess what brings me in is... well, my supervisor thought it would be a good idea if I came to talk to someone. I work as a personal care aide, and we had this staff meeting the other day. I just... I got a little bit passionate, I suppose? I hope that's okay to say. We were talking about safety, and I got pretty worked up and just started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill. 

I was really just trying to be helpful and make sure everyone understood. But I was moving chairs around and waving my arms to show how to catch somebody, and... well, I guess I couldn't seem to stop doing it, even when folks told me to sit down and take a breath. I just wanted to do a good job, you know? Does that... does that make sense why they'd want me to come here?
Can you tell me if there are times when people around you have said your behavior seemed strange or didn’t make sense, even when you felt you were doing the right thing?

Well, um... I guess that's sort of what I was just talking about with that staff meeting. I hope it's okay to bring that up again. To me, I was doing the right thing, you know? Keeping the patients safe is just so important. 

But... yeah, I suppose when I was moving all those chairs around and waving my arms to show how to catch somebody... they probably thought it didn't make sense to do all that right then. Especially since I couldn't seem to just stop and sit down when they asked me to. I really didn't mean to make anyone uncomfortable or act out of turn, I promise. I was just trying so hard to be helpful and show I cared about my job. I hope you don't think badly of me for it. Is... is that the kind of example you were looking for, doctor?
Can you tell me if there have been times when you believed something strongly, even when others told you it wasn't true or didn't make sense?

Um, well... I guess there is something, but I really hope it doesn't make me sound, you know, paranoid or anything. I try to get along with everybody, I really do. 

But sometimes... even when I'm feeling totally calm and just doing my work, I get this really strong feeling that my supervisor and a couple of the other aides are... well, keeping notes on me. Like they're testing me. They'll make these little comments that seem normal, but I just feel sure they're trying to prove I'm not safe to be around the seniors. 

I haven't really brought it up because I don't want to cause trouble, and maybe I'm just reading too much into things because I want to be a good employee. But it just feels so real to me. Does that... does that sound like what you were asking about? I hope I'm answering your questions right.

Can you tell me more about that feeling that your supervisor and others are keeping notes on you and testing you — has this belief ever changed or gone away, even for a little while, or does it seem completely real to you all the time?

Um, well... I hope it's okay to say this, because I really don't want to sound like a difficult person to work with. But... honestly, it feels pretty real to me pretty much all the time. 

Even when my mood is totally fine, you know? Like, when I'm just calm and having a normal day, I still get that feeling. I just feel sure that they're watching me and taking down notes, testing me with those little comments they make. It really feels like they're just waiting to prove I'm not safe around the seniors. 

I try to just keep my head down and do a good job, because I really care about the patients. But that feeling doesn't really go away. I know it probably sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud... I just hope you don't think I'm crazy or anything for feeling that way. Does that answer your question okay?
Can you tell me if there have been times when you've questioned whether this belief about being tested is true, or if it's something you've never doubted at all?

Well, um... I really try to be open-minded, I do. I want to be a team player. But... honestly, I don't really doubt it. I know I probably should, and I hope you don't think I'm just being stubborn. 

It's just that... like I said, even when I'm totally calm, not upset or anything, I still feel absolutely sure that my supervisor and those couple of people are keeping notes on me. I just know they're testing me with those little comments, trying to prove I'm not safe around the seniors. It just feels so real, I can't really talk myself out of it. I'm sorry if that's not the right way to think about it... I'm really trying to be honest with you. Is it okay that I feel that way?
